evidence.finding: Billing skill mappings were updated at 09:15, exactly at incident start.
Billing staffing fell from 12 to 9 agents while General Service increased from 19 to 22 at the incident boundary.
Billing mean service level fell from 89.84% to 44.70%, while General Service improved from 92.14% to 96.48%.
Billing offered volume increased 26.89%, compounding its reduced capacity.
Center scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49; productive staffing changed only -0.28% on average.
Reported center service level dropped below the 80% target beginning at incident onset, including 67.06% at 09:15 and 59.14% at 09:30.

primary_root_cause_detail: The 09:15 Billing skill-mapping change redistributed three staffed agents from Billing to General Service, creating a localized Billing capacity imbalance. Billing service level then collapsed while General Service improved. Moderate Billing volume growth amplified the impact.
recommended_actions: Restore or correct the pre-incident Billing skill mappings and validate agent eligibility before deployment.
Return sufficient staffed capacity to Billing and monitor queue depth, ASA, abandonment, and service level until recovery.
Add pre-deployment routing validation and post-change queue-level guardrails that alert on abrupt staffing redistribution.
Apply temporary overflow support to Billing during forecast or observed volume increases.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: No broad demand surge was established; General Service volume declined while its service level improved. Billing's increase was moderate and contributory.
Center-wide scheduled and logged-in headcount remained stable, and Billing's three-agent loss was mirrored by General Service's gain.
Billing mean AHT decreased 0.49% after incident start rather than increasing.
All reported center service levels matched the specified formula exactly, with zero recalculation variance.

stakeholder_summary: A Billing routing configuration change at 09:15 redirected effective capacity away from Billing, causing a localized queue imbalance and service-level failure. Overall staffing was stable, AHT did not increase, and the reported metrics were valid. Moderate Billing volume growth worsened the impact but was not the primary cause.
